definition: Merriam-Webster's Word of the Day for November 20, 2026 is: ruthless &#149; \ROOTH-lus\&nbsp; &#149; adjective Ruthless means "having no pity." It describes people, behaviors, circumstances, etc. regarded as cruel or merciless. // Wolves and other large carnivores are often portrayed (and feared) as ruthless predators even as they play vital roles in their ecosystems. See the entry > Examples: "One of Shakespeare's most powerful and enduring tragedies, 'Macbeth' remains an urgent and gripping story. Ambition and prophecy collide as a fateful prediction drives Macbeth into a ruthless pursuit of power, destroying everything in his path." — The Daily Gazette (Schenectady, New York), 25 Sept. 2026
did_you_know: ? Ruthless can be defined as "without ruth" or "having no ruth." So what, then, is ruth? The noun ruth , which is now considerably less common than ruthless , means "compassion for the misery of another," "sorrow for one's own faults," or "remorse." And, just as it is possible for one to be without ruth, it is also possible to be full of ruth. The antonym of ruthless is ruthful , meaning "full of ruth" or "tender." Ruthful can also mean "full of sorrow" or "causing sorrow." Ruth traces back to the Middle English noun ruthe , itself from ruwen , meaning "to affect with sorrow, be sorrowful, rue ."
